newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria to try looters of public enterprises.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria to try looters of public enterprises.

text.p: Nigeria's military government said on Wednesday a decree to punish people who ruined state-owned companies would go into effect soon.

The attorney-general's office said in a statement that a public enterprises tribunal would try offences such as embezzling funds, mismanagement and inflated or faked contracts. Convicts would have right of appeal to a special appeals tribunal.
"The offences covered by the decree includes contributing to the economic adversity of public enterprises and failure to execute contracts," the statement said.

The decree, signed last November by military ruler General Sani Abacha, takes effect from November 17, 1993 when he siezed power in the chaos unleashed by annulment of a presidential election to restore civil rule.

Abacha, who has since been cleaning up the corruption-ridden banking sector through a failed banks decree under which scores of bankers and people who took unpaid loans have been jailed and made to refund the money, had vowed to extend the crusade to other areas of the economy.

In his 1997 fiscal budget broadcast last month, he said that hundreds of millions of dollars had been looted from state-owned enterprises, many of which were not functioning properly and that this should not go unpunished.
Lawyers said the Public Enterprises Regulatory Commission Decree, as the latest law is titled, would rope in hundreds of present and past officials of government establishments.
"You will soon see many rich people fleeing from the country to escape the decree," said Bola Oke, a lawyer.

According to the official statement "The jurisdiction of the tribunal shall not be affected by the fact that a person charged has resigned, had his appointment terminated or has otherwise left the employment of the public enterprise."
It did not spell out the punishment to be meted.
Nigerian public enterprises range from oil and gas to power, steel, telecommunications and several other sectors.
